title: Unveiling the latest Gemma model advancements: Kathleen Kenealy
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind research engineer announces the Gemma 2 open model family (9B and 27B), PaliGemma multimodal, RecurrentGemma, and CodeGemma, emphasizing benchmark performance, framework compatibility, and fine-tuning ease. The talk is a product launch with no engineering methodology, workflow, or agent-system techniques.

takeaways.technique: Small-model capability check before routing to large models
takeaways.what_they_do: They claim a 27B model performs in the ballpark of much larger models on benchmarks and human evals, implying a smaller model can substitute for a larger one on many tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our 27b model is has performance in the same ballpark as llama 370b
takeaways.numbers: 27B vs 70B comparison; claims 2-3x larger model parity

takeaways.technique: Human preference evals alongside academic benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: They note benchmarks are not always indicative of real-world performance and run extensive human evaluations, finding their models preferred over larger ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes these benchmarks are not always indicative of how a model will perform once it's in your hands
